questions.q: Why does Tracy retell the story of the blind monks and the elephant?
a: To show that we often see only part of the whole
To argue that experts rarely agree on facts
To explain why teamwork beats solo effort
To prove that our senses can deceive us
questions.why: The first lesson says each monk is partly right but none of them grasps the entire animal.

questions.q: What does the summary say about the idea that we use only 10% of our brain?
a: It is a myth, since we use all of it over a day
It is true for most adults
It applies only to creative work
It was confirmed by recent scans
questions.why: The first lesson says we do not fire every cell at once, but across 24 hours we use 100%.

questions.q: How does Kahneman describe the mind's two systems?
a: Fast and intuitive versus slow and deliberate
Emotional versus logical
Conscious versus unconscious
Creative versus mechanical
questions.why: The second lesson says new information lands in the fast system and needs effort to reach the slow one.

questions.q: How much time does Tracy suggest spending each day on your long-term goals?
a: Ten minutes
Five minutes
Thirty minutes
One hour
questions.why: The second lesson says ten minutes a day planning your next five years pays off.

questions.q: What are Tracy's three safeguards against mechanical thinking?
a: Be clear, be focused, concentrate
Be fast, be bold, be busy
Be curious, be patient, be kind
Be honest, be humble, be calm
questions.why: The third lesson says to set simple goals, do fewer things better and design your environment.
